confirmed.claim: Imports from `typeorm/browser` instead of `typeorm` — this is the browser bundle and cannot use Node.js pg drivers; app crashes on startup
`typeorm` version pinned to `^1.0.0` — no such version exists (latest stable is 0.3.x); npm install fails to resolve it
Missing `database` field in database config — TypeORM cannot connect to PostgreSQL without a target database name
Uses `DATABASE_USER` env var but the rest of the app and .env-example use `DATABASE_USERNAME` — migration CLI connects with undefined username
DTO has `firstname`/`lastname` (all lowercase) but User entity has `firstName`/`lastName` (camelCase) — spread into create() saves undefined for those columns, causing NOT NULL constraint violations
`LoginDto extends PartialType(RegisterDto)` — inherits username/firstName/lastName validators; with `forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, any extra fields from clients throw 400; semantically wrong design
`@Controller()` missing route prefix (should be 'users'); `findById` returns null which is sent as HTTP 200 null body instead of throwing 404

Swagger config missing `addBearerAuth()` so `@ApiBearerAuth()` decorators have no effect in Swagger UI — cannot test authenticated endpoints. Also `ValidationPipe` was registered AFTER Swagger setup, risking unvalidated requests during document generation.
Redundant `revoked: boolean` column that is never updated (repository only sets `revokedAt`) — always stays `false`, misleads auditors and wastes storage
`findActiveByUser` doesn't filter `expiresAt > NOW()` — expired but non-revoked tokens are included in active sessions, causing unnecessary argon2 hash comparisons
`createAt`/`updateAt` are typos — should be `createdAt`/`updatedAt`. Propagates wrong field names to API responses and Swagger docs.

Wrong JWT env var names (`JWT_ACCESS`, `JWT_REFRESH`, `JWT_EXPIRY_TIME`) — a developer copying .env-example gets `undefined` secrets; JWT is then signed with `undefined` as the key, which is a critical security vulnerability
`AppController` and `AppService` are defined but not registered in `AppModule` — NestJS cannot inject `AppService` into `AppController`, throwing a DI error at startup

`generateSignedUploadParams` fetches config key `cloudinary.webhookurl` but the config registers it as `cloudinary.notificationUrl`. With `getOrThrow`, this throws on every avatar upload URL request — the entire signed-URL flow is broken.
Port is read from `process.env.REDIS_HOST` instead of `process.env.REDIS_PORT`. `parseInt('localhost')` → NaN — BullMQ connects to `host:NaN` and silently fails to process any queue jobs.

`WebhooksModule` (containing the Cloudinary webhook controller + BullMQ queue injection) was never imported into `AppModule`. The `POST /webhooks/cloudinary` route didn't exist — Cloudinary could never trigger BullMQ jobs.

Class exported as `webhooksModule` (lowercase 'w') — violates NestJS PascalCase convention, causes misleading DI debug messages, and mismatches the import in app.module.ts which now uses `WebhooksModule`.

`publicId.split('/')[1]` has no validation — if `publicId` is malformed (no slash or empty segment), `userId` is `undefined` or `''`, causing TypeORM to update the wrong row or crash the processor silently.
Unused `import { config } from 'process'` — dead import that shadows the `config: ConfigService` parameter name in `BullModule.forRootAsync` useFactory, potentially causing confusion.
